label: humane technology
description: A recurring engineering theme where systems are evaluated by whether they reduce harm, preserve dignity, and make interfaces calmer or more supportive.

label: accessibility and adaptive interfaces
description: Accessibility appears as concrete product architecture: neurodivergent support surfaces, multilingual/offline-first constraints, cognitive accessibility, and calmer UI patterns.

label: backend systems and scalable APIs
description: Several projects use REST API surfaces, modular services, optimized inference paths, and backend-oriented data modeling.

label: graph theory and optimization
description: Graph theory is both a DSA focus and an applied project pattern, most directly visible in DelAI's weighted graph routing system.

label: AI safety and practical ML
description: AI appears as applied classification, safety detection, study tooling, crop-disease detection, and risk analysis rather than as a generic chatbot layer.

label: interface psychology
description: The archive repeatedly treats UI/UX as a systems concern: component architecture, emotional load, visual consistency, and interaction choices shape how the software behaves.
